title: Whole Grain Pasta with Tomato Sauce, Seafood, and Vegetables

content.title: About
content.content: Whole grain pasta with tomato‑based sauce, seafood and added vegetables is a balanced dish that combines complex carbohydrates, protein from seafood, and vitamins from vegetables. The sauce is made from ripe tomatoes, olive oil and aromatic herbs, while the seafood mix includes shrimp, mussels and calamari, complemented by broccoli, carrots and sweet bell pepper.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Whole grain pasta provides more fiber and micronutrients than traditional white‑flour pasta.
Tomatoes used in the sauce are rich in lycopene, an antioxidant that supports heart health.
Seafood is an excellent source of omega‑3 fatty acids, which benefit brain function.
Broccoli and bell pepper add vitamin C, which enhances iron absorption from the pasta.
In Italy the dish is traditionally served as “seafood spaghetti,” but here whole grain pasta offers a healthier twist.

items.title: Supports Digestion
items.content: The fiber in whole grain pasta promotes intestinal motility and helps you feel full longer.

items.title: Antioxidant Protection
items.content: Lycopene from tomatoes and vitamin C from vegetables help neutralize free radicals.

items.title: Heart Health
items.content: Omega‑3s from seafood lower triglyceride levels and support normal blood pressure.

items.title: Immune Support
items.content: Vitamins A and C, along with zinc from seafood, strengthen the immune system.

items.title: Rich Protein Source
items.content: Seafood combined with whole grain pasta provides a complete set of essential amino acids.

items.title: Seafood Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to shrimp, mussels or calamari.

items.title: High Sodium Content
items.content: Tomato sauce often contains added salt; people monitoring sodium intake should watch portion size.

items.title: Food Interactions
items.content: Omega‑3s can enhance the effect of anticoagulant medications; consult a doctor if you take such drugs.

items.title: Gluten Content
items.content: Whole grain pasta contains gluten and is not suitable for those with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the pasta hot, tossed with the sauce and seafood. Optionally garnish with fresh basil, grated Parmesan, or a drizzle of olive oil. A squeeze of lemon adds a bright acidity.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store dry whole grain pasta in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. Cooked pasta with sauce and seafood should be kept in the refrigerator for no more than 2 days and reheated to at least 75 °C.
